event.summary: Removal of old tmux status and tab discovery is specified retirement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Existing terminals in the private tmux server no longer report through these status classifiers, and old tabs no longer appear in replies. Considered the resulting loss of running agents and terminal history. Could-be-highest: yes, since removal of still-running terminals can lose user processes and terminal contents. Suggested bucket if contrary to contract: highest. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance; source retirement/startup correspondence still being checked. proposed_drop: exact acceptance in SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3003–3016: "This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program." The same paragraph says "A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them" and explicitly accepts that a failure to stop the old server may leave a second agent on Restart. The status.rs patch removes KnownTmuxNames, pane_evidence, old tab discovery, and dead_pane_exit_code while preserving host evidence/classification. possible_cover: none searched. Evidence is source and contract only, no execution. Next check: retirement conversion/startup ordering must make host-only status safe for old rows.

event.summary: Retired tmux status and tab discovery follows explicitly accepted process loss
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Retiring private-tmux terminals can terminate running agents, close old tabs and discard terminal screens/history. This release deliberately treats those terminals as ended even if teardown fails, so Restart can create a second agent beside one that survived. Could-be-highest: yes, established process/history loss. Suggested bucket: highest if explicit acceptance is rejected. Confidence: confirmed source behavior and specification acceptance, source-only. proposed_drop: SPEC.md:3006–3010 says "This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program" and "its terminal's last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed". SPEC.md:3013–3016 says "A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them" and explicitly accepts Restart beside a surviving old agent. SPEC_impl.md:2891–2927 specifies retirement before reload, terminal-less old rows, Interrupted conversion for active outcomes, and preservation of ended outcomes. Source: service/core.rs:6142–6184 ends old terminals before reload; :6675–6679 never resolves old pane addresses; :6769–6782 reads direct generation-scoped sentinel evidence before :6805–6822 converts remaining active old rows to Interrupted. :6635–6645 separately adopts host tabs for every session, including old-kind agent rows, so old-agent conversion does not itself discard host tabs. Removing pane_evidence and old tab discovery from status.rs follows that replacement contract. possible_cover: caller reports likely duplicate coverage in g099/g110/g113/g118; no coverage sources were read here. The parent has accepted no drop; retain this as a potentially highest finding proposed for drop and independent checking. No implementation violation is established. Original strongest consequences preserved: terminating user processes, losing terminal content, and possible second agent after failed teardown. No runtime execution or unresolved source premise.

exact_cover_quotes: SPEC.md:3000-3004: A supervisor that finds that tmux server when it starts ends it, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program. A session whose agent was still launching, running or being stopped in one becomes interrupted, as after a reboot, and gets the notice Status describes; one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal's last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed.

SPEC.md:3008-3011: A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them. A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.

The earlier records proposed specification acceptance; none was a parent-approved drop. All are preserved here.
returned_claim_checks.proposed_basis: Exact specification acceptance, not rarity, a filter, or an assertion that process/history loss is harmless. Parent must submit this proposed covered disposition to the independent drop check before dismissal.

event.summary: Removing the capture budget does not remove a host-output attribution guard
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Failed-launch details still quote only that launch's final screen; removing the tmux capture budget does not expose a later launch's output or introduce a new blocking capture operation for hosts. Considered consequence: stale observer quoting another run's output or repeated captures delaying fleet observation. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; the considered direct consequences were misleading diagnostics or delayed status. Suggested bucket if established: other (diagnostics), high if material sustained fleet delay were established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: parent revision launch_artifacts.rs:78–95 already used an unbudgeted synchronous host screen read before the tmux capture budget, while current launch_artifacts.rs:59–76 retains the same host.evidence Owned/dead check and memory-only screen read. The status.rs change at :652 only removes the retired tmux-specific branch/async signature. SPEC_impl.md:2755–2766 states: "A host runs one child for its whole life, so everything on its screen is this launch's output; the screen is quoted only once the host's exit record has been processed, which follows the child's drained output". hosts/terminal.rs:835–850 reports dead only for processed Exited state, so the observer's terminal_dead and excerpt's second check preserve final-output ordering. possible_cover: none searched. No execution; this is source and contract analysis. No unresolved premise remains for this candidate.

event.summary: Removing the capture budget does not remove a host-output attribution guard
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Removing the old tmux capture timeout/budget does not introduce a new synchronous host capture or let an obsolete observer quote a later host's launch. Considered consequences: misleading launch diagnostics, later-launch output attribution, or sustained fleet observation delay. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; suggested bucket if established: other for diagnostics, high for material sustained fleet delay. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of this change-specific concern, with exact boundary clarified during synthesis. proposed_drop: baseline launch_artifacts.rs:78–95 already read host.screen_tail synchronously and without the tmux budget; current :59–76 keeps that host-only path, so status.rs:652 removes only the obsolete tmux async capture plumbing. Current host evidence is Owned/dead only after Liveness::Exited, not merely after an OS process probe reports dead (hosts/terminal.rs:818–850). The ordered runtime dispatch handles output/resizes/gaps before Exited (:3342–3370); on_exited (:3929–3942) flushes an open synchronized update and publishes it before setting Exited. Thus the observer's terminal_dead at status.rs:610–611 and append_launch_excerpt's second dead check do not quote an earlier process-probe boundary. Clarification: Exited does not promise an immutable screen forever; :3929–3931 explicitly continues feeding later descendant output from the same launch. That does not attribute another run's host screen. SPEC_impl.md:2760–2762 says "A host runs one child for its whole life, so everything on its screen is this launch's output; the screen is quoted only once the host's exit record has been processed, which follows the child's drained output". Current observe_entry reads the generation-specific sentinel before wrapper inference, while pending Stop suppresses that inference; the cache's applies_to check and store.rs:498–528 reject a late inferred error during Stop and all errors after annotated exit. possible_cover: caller says g100 independently checks bounded screen-tail copying; this record does not decide that distinct resource-bound issue or claim a parent-approved drop. No runtime execution. No unresolved premise remains for the removal-of-budget concern.

event.summary: Removing the capture budget preserves the existing processed-exit boundary
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Removing the tmux capture budget does not introduce a new synchronous host capture or make an obsolete observer quote a later launch's host. Considered consequences remain misleading launch diagnostics, wrong-run output attribution, or sustained fleet observation delay. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Suggested bucket if established: other for diagnostics, high for material sustained fleet delay. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the change-specific capture concern; exact drain boundary now checked through producer, journal and consumer. proposed_drop: baseline launch_artifacts.rs:78–95 already read host.screen_tail synchronously without the tmux budget; current :59–76 retains that path. hosts/terminal.rs:818–850 distinguishes OS-probe dead from processed Exited; status evidence remains live until the latter. terminal-host/src/host.rs:454–485 reaps the child, drains available pty output, then journals exit once the drain empties or reaches its time/byte bound. terminal-host/SPEC.md:134–141 specifies: "It then reads whatever output is already available, bounded by EXIT_DRAIN_TIME and EXIT_DRAIN_BYTES, appends an exit record with the child's exit status or terminating signal at the current offset, and goes on"; :456–457 gives 200 ms and 4 MiB. terminal-host/src/journal.rs:418–427 sends Exited only after the stream cursor reaches that record's byte and resize position. hosts/terminal.rs:3342–3370 applies records in stream order, and :3929–3942 flushes an open synchronized update before setting Exited. status.rs:610–611 and launch_artifacts.rs:66–72 therefore use the processed bounded-drain boundary, not merely process death. Important caveat retained: this is not proof that every future byte or all output beyond the drain bounds has reached the screen. Descendants may continue writing after Exited, and the same host's screen may change; that remains same-launch output and was already possible in the baseline. SPEC_impl.md:2760–2762 attributes output by one-child-per-host lifetime and requires processed exit before quoting. The generation-scoped direct sentinel precedes wrapper inference, pending Stop suppresses inference, and store.rs:498–528 rejects late inferred Stop errors and errors after annotated exit. possible_cover: caller says g100 independently checks bounded screen-tail copying, a distinct issue this record does not decide. No parent-approved drop, no runtime execution, and no unresolved premise for removal of the old budget.

event.summary: Capture-budget removal adds no new host capture; inherited-history attribution is a separate existing route
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Original TLDR/consequences preserved: failed-launch diagnostics might quote another run's output, or repeated captures might delay fleet observation. Suggested bucket if established: other for misleading diagnostics, high for material sustained fleet delay. Could-be-highest: no demonstrated security or user-work-loss route. Confidence: confirmed source/range analysis, no execution. proposed_drop remains proposed, with two narrow source bases: removal of the tmux budget does not introduce synchronous/unbudgeted host capture, and the inherited-history resize path was already present at the exclusive range base. The earlier blanket assertion that one child plus a blank seed excludes all previous-run text is retracted; it was too strong. No parent drop or lowering has been accepted. possible_cover: refreshed neighbour g009/l1 investigates this same inherited-history resize concern; g013/f2 is its supplied cross-reference; g100 owns bounded screen-tail copying, distinct from the removed timeout budget.

Checks resolving the reopened lead: current host_restart.rs:216–255 supplies old host history/size to the new host, :418–490 obtains that history seed. snapshot/v1/paint.rs:401–436 paints primary history above a blank screen but does not tag inherited rows as non-current. vendor/alacritty_terminal/src/grid/resize.rs:41–71 grows the visible area by pulling rows from history, and term/mod.rs:735–758 delegates height growth to it. handlers.rs:1910 and :2060–2082 resize the selected attached host; hosts/terminal.rs:2344–2353 admits valid resizes while its runtime exists without testing whether the launch spec was consumed or the child exited. :3871–3884 applies the resize to the emulator. screen_tail at :2229–2240 reads the visible text, and launch_artifacts.rs:59–76 quotes it after processed exit without tracking inherited-row provenance. Consequently the blank initial screen alone does not prove that a later visible-screen excerpt excludes old seeded history; grid growth can put it there. This is diagnostic attribution, not selection of another host or a later generation's runtime. Processing Exited after the bounded 200ms/4MiB drain still establishes the previously checked ordering, but neither that ordering nor one-child-per-host identity excludes rows inherited in the seed. Later descendant output remains another same-launch screen mutability caveat.

Whole-range attribution: exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a already contains the unbudgeted host branch of append_launch_excerpt at launch_artifacts.rs:78–95, including host.screen_tail and the same processed-exit check; its status.rs:877–885 invokes it for wrapper failures. Base host_restart.rs:414 onward accepts a seed and :650 onward reads old.history_seed. Base emulator.rs:224–227 has the same resize forwarding, and the grid grow-lines implementation is byte-unchanged from base to reviewed commit. The complete base-to-reviewed paint.rs diff removes only an unused SGR helper at :743, leaving paint_history unchanged. Thus the ordinary host budget, blank-history seed and grid-promotion mechanisms already coexist before the full pinned range. This assigned status.rs edit removes tmux parameters/async plumbing while retaining those host contracts. Source refutes a newly introduced capture-budget or inherited-history mechanism in this assigned change; it does not refute the existing diagnostic concern or the neighbour's review of newly generalized documentation. No independent emulator audit is claimed. Suggested direction if that separate concern is retained: account for inherited history after resize, rather than treating blank-at-birth as a permanent provenance guarantee. The c2 lead is resolved to this candidate; no readily checkable premise remains for its change-attribution judgment.

event.summary: Exit-enrichment test documentation conflates probe death with observer evidence
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: The rewritten test documentation teaches the wrong lifecycle boundary: it says a host observation first sees death without a code because the process probe precedes the exit record, but these observations deliberately do not consume that probe. This can mislead maintainers about when status/launch classification may treat a terminal as dead. No runtime misclassification is established. Details: status.rs:1053–1057 newly says "a host terminal's probe says dead before its exit record arrives" and therefore "the observation that first sees the death can have no code while the next one does". The only production caller of this observation function is observe_entry at :704; it obtains live from terminal_evidence at :580–604, which calls host.evidence at :124–127. hosts/terminal.rs:835–850 makes Running evidence dead:false until the complete ChildExit has been processed, then reports dead:true and maps its code together. probe at :818–827 can report Dead earlier but is not this observer's input. Signal death yields no code (:853–859, :886–889), rather than a temporarily unread exit code for that same host. The test at :1060–1067 hand-builds dead/no-code and dead/code inputs; its assertions still test monotonic enrichment of an already stored unknown code, but do not demonstrate the claimed within-host observation sequence. Correct production ordering does not make the new explanation accurate. The documented processed-exit boundary in SPEC_impl.md:2703–2704, :2760–2762 and hosts/terminal.rs:835–837 is the governing contract.

Attribution and persistence: exclusive-base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a and the immediate parent describe tmux publishing pane_dead before pane_dead_status (base status.rs:1303–1306, parent :1298–1301). The assigned commit replaces that tmux rationale with the incorrect host rationale. The only later in-range status.rs change is f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e; pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db retains the exact false explanation at :1033–1037. Suggested fix: explain enrichment of previously stored incomplete outcomes, and preserve the distinction between lifecycle process probes and processed exit evidence rather than suggesting the observation uses probe death.

Suggested bucket: other (newly inaccurate test/lifecycle documentation). Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security/user-work-loss route from this documentation itself. Confidence: confirmed source/caller/range analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: no matching item in supplied discovery-neighbours.json; no forbidden coverage search. Caveats: this does not claim the enrichment test should be deleted or that enrichment is unreachable for an existing stored unknown outcome. It concerns the newly asserted reason for the test. All readily checkable premises above settled; l3 is resolved from lead to finding.

Details: production docstring status.rs:179–181 newly describes liveness as "the host's child has not exited — a fact". The rewritten enrichment-test docstring :1053–1057 says "a host terminal's probe says dead before its exit record arrives" and therefore "the observation that first sees the death can have no code while the next one does". These are two manifestations of the same conflation. The only production caller of observation is observe_entry at :704, which obtains live from terminal_evidence at :580–604; :124–127 calls host.evidence, not probe. hosts/terminal.rs:835–850 explicitly keeps Running evidence dead:false until the complete ChildExit is processed, then publishes dead:true and maps the code together. probe at :818–827 can return Dead before that, but is not this observer's input. The only later in-range status.rs commit is f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e, whose diff only removes terminal-kind reply fields/helper and leaves both explanations.
